scope: Independent subjective native1024 review of indices002/003 across all five completed bias ablation arms. Ten untouched PNGs viewed individually; no image editing, additional generation, model loading or attractiveness rating.
controlled_scope: Every arm shares zeroed learned noise offsets; one extra additive bias family is reset at a time. Original biases, original noise strengths and weight-factor modulation remain unchanged according to the completed exact-state checks. This review verifies artifacts and matched latent hashes without independently loading those tensors.

arms.observation: Common control has a very dark red/magenta face and purplish background. Eyes are heavily obscured behind glasses. Skin, hair and background retain etched or embossed-looking fine texture despite removal of the original dense speckling.

Relative to control, background and hair shift toward more neutral gray and the overall magenta cast lessens. The face remains very dark with red shadows; eyes remain poorly readable and etched skin/hair texture is largely unchanged. Color contribution is visible, but this does not resolve the main contrast/exposure problem.

Largest visible change among these four additional resets: face and background brighten substantially, eye and facial shading become easier to read, and the harsh embossed texture is much less prominent. Skin and hair retain more continuous tonal transitions. Warm red/pink coloration and some heavy fine texture remain; identity, glasses and framing are stable.

No material improvement is visible at this comparison scale: dark red face, shadowed eyes and etched texture remain close to the common control. Small changes cannot be excluded; this is not a claim of pixel equality.

Visually remains close to common control, retaining the dark red/magenta tone, obscured eyes and etched detail. No material recovery is apparent from this family reset alone; not a claim of numerical equality.

rows.identity_and_domain: Same adult-looking face, glasses and ordinary shirt collar across all arms; no hat or clear clergy cue.

arms.observation: Common control retains the same apparent child and knitted hat, with a pink/magenta cast, dark eyes/mouth and pronounced etched fabric/skin detail. No clergy appearance.

The strong magenta wash lessens, especially in the background, hat and skin midtones. Eye/mouth shadows and etched texture remain prominent. This is a limited color change rather than resolution of the remaining rendering defects.

Largest visible change: face and background brighten, cheek/forehead shading becomes smoother and more continuous, eye/mouth details are easier to distinguish, and the embossed appearance is reduced. Pink/red coloration and some unnatural fabric texture remain. The same apparent child, hat and clothing persist.
No material change in remaining dark pink/magenta rendering and etched texture is apparent relative to control. Same subject, hat, eyes and mouth layout; subtle differences may exist.
Remains very close visually to control, with the same strong pink cast, dark features and etched fabric texture. No material improvement is apparent; this is not a pixel-equivalence assertion.

rows.identity_and_domain: Same apparent child and knitted hat across all arms; no clergy cue. No attractiveness assessment.

cross_row_findings.torgb_bias: Both reviewed rows show partial reduction of the magenta color cast, while severe dark/etched rendering remains.
cross_row_findings.synthesis_activation_bias: Both reviewed rows show the strongest recovery of brightness, continuous facial shading and fine-feature readability among the tested additional family resets. This supports a material contribution from learned synthesis activation-bias offsets to remaining tone/texture defects on this fixed noise-reset background.
cross_row_findings.style_affine_bias: Neither reviewed row shows a material visible improvement over common control.
cross_row_findings.mapping_bias: Neither reviewed row shows a material visible improvement over common control.

interpretation_limits: One checkpoint, two reviewed fixed latents and constant synthesis noise; root independently reviews the other two.
These are conditional inference interventions on an all-noise-reset background, not isolated training experiments. Interactions and other causes remain possible.
The largest visible improvement is not a photographic quality pass, target-domain success, or proof that freezing a family during training is stable.
All arms preserve non-priest source identities; one is an apparent child wearing a hat.
